concepts.definition: Two signals that are not simultaneous but shifted 90 degrees from each other. Together they give both the step and the direction.
concepts.example: Clockwise, the states change in the order 11, 01, 00, 10 (CLK, DT).
concepts.pitfall: Looking only at CLK: it falls the same way in both directions, so you cannot tell the direction.

concepts.definition: When CLK falls, look at DT: if DT is 1 it is one direction (sayac++), if it is 0 the other direction (sayac--).
concepts.example: If DT is still 1 when CLK falls from 1 to 0, sayac goes up.
concepts.pitfall: Mixing up CLK and DT: the direction comes out reversed.

concepts.definition: Running a short function (ISR) as soon as a pin edge happens, without waiting for loop().
concepts.example: attachInterrupt(digitalPinToInterrupt(2), adim, FALLING); when CLK falls, adim() runs.
concepts.pitfall: Connecting CLK to a pin other than D2 or D3: on the Uno the interrupt does not work.

concepts.definition: Tells the compiler that the variable can change outside the normal program flow, for example in an interrupt.
concepts.example: volatile int sayac = 0; is used both in the ISR and in loop().
concepts.pitfall: Not writing volatile: loop() may not see the change.

concepts.definition: Ignoring an edge if at least a certain time has not passed between two edges.
concepts.example: If the micros() difference is less than 2000 µs, the edge is skipped.
concepts.pitfall: Making the threshold too large: when you turn fast, real ticks are thrown away too.

quiz.explanation: In the opposite direction, when CLK falls from 10 to 00, DT is already 0, so sayac-- runs on every tick: 5 - 2 = 3. Clockwise, DT would be 1 and sayac would be 7.

quiz.prompt: The lab's encoder applies one state change every simulated millisecond, and one tick is 4 changes. If you move the Position property from 0 to 30 in one go, in how many ms does the encoder finish its movement?
quiz.explanation: 30 ticks x 4 changes = 120 changes, and each takes 1 ms: 120 ms. That means 4 ms per tick (at most 250 ticks/s); the bounce threshold must be chosen smaller than these 4 ms.

On the Uno only D2 and D3 are interrupt pins. digitalPinToInterrupt(4) does not give a valid interrupt, so the ISR never runs. CLK must be connected to D2 (or D3). volatile and INPUT_PULLUP are correct.

quiz.prompt: Why can a program that looks only at the CLK signal not find the direction of rotation?
options: The CLK signal is too fast
CLK falls in the same way in both directions; the state of DT at that moment decides the direction
The encoder only turns in one direction
quiz.explanation: CLK falls from 1 to 0 both clockwise and in the opposite direction. The difference is whether DT is 1 or 0 at the moment of the fall; that is why both signals are read together.

quiz.prompt: The encoder is turned fast and CLK falls every 4 ms. The threshold ARALIK_US = 6000 was chosen. Over 20 falls in a row, how many ticks does the program count? (The first edge is accepted.)
quiz.explanation: The accepted edge is at t = 0; the next one comes 4 ms later and is thrown away because it is less than 6 ms; the one that comes 8 ms later is accepted. Every second edge is counted: 20 / 2 = 10. If the threshold were smaller than 4 ms (for example 2 ms), 20 would be counted; when the threshold is too large, real ticks are lost.
